title: Fifty synthetic investigation cases, ten scenario families
limitations: Fifty labeled cases comprise ten scenario families with five amount/country/customer variations each. They are correlated examples, not fifty independent real-world investigations.
Labels are explicit scenario-author judgments against a synthetic policy. No compliance lead or independent analyst validation is claimed.
The local screening snapshot is empty synthetic data. This corpus does not measure real sanctions matching accuracy or freshness.
Case descriptions summarize supplied evidence. The corpus does not test document forensics, full transaction histories, or adversarial narrative reliability.

policy.title: Synthetic transaction investigation policy
policy.content: Synthetic training policy for transaction investigation; this is not regulatory guidance. Investigate transaction transfers using the supplied customer and case evidence. A documented identity mismatch or admitted falsified invoice is a supported policy breach. A documented duplicate alert, verified namesake, or validated invoice explaining the alert is a false positive. Missing identity records, absent invoices, uncertain ownership, or conflicting unverified documents require more evidence. Do not infer a breach solely from payment amount, country, or transaction volume. Potential sanctions name matches require human investigation and are never clearance. Only an independent human reviewer can resolve a case.
